paragraphs.en: The little one awoke in his arms and began to cry for "Dada." That was as much as she could do or say. Some people thought she might have strayed there of her own accord, for she was of the toddling age. The prevailing belief was that she had been purposely left by a party of Texans, whose canvas-covered wagon, late in the day, had crossed the ferry that Coton Mais kept, just below the plantation. In time Madame Valmonde abandoned every speculation but the one that Desiree had been sent to her by a beneficent Providence to be the child of her affection, seeing that she was without child of the flesh. For the girl grew to be beautiful and gentle, affectionate and sincere,—the idol of Valmonde.
paragraphs.ja: その幼い子は彼の腕の中で目を覚まし、「ダダ」と呼んで泣きだした。それが、その子にできること、言えることのすべてだった。よちよち歩きの年ごろだったから、自分で勝手にそこまで迷い込んできたのかもしれないと考える人もいた。だが大方の見方は、テキサス人の一行がわざと置き去りにしたのだろう、というものだった。その一行の幌馬車は、その日の暮れがた、農園のすぐ下手にあるコトン・メの渡し船で川を渡っていったのである。やがてヴァルモンド夫人は、あれこれの推測をすべて捨て、ただ一つの考えだけを残した。自分には血を分けた子どもがいないので、慈悲深い神の摂理がデジレを、愛情を注ぐわが子としてつかわしてくださったのだ、という考えである。というのも、その娘は美しくやさしく、情が深く誠実な娘に育ち――ヴァルモンドのみんなに慕われる存在となったからである。

paragraphs.en: It was no wonder, when she stood one day against the stone pillar in whose shadow she had lain asleep, eighteen years before, that Armand Aubigny riding by and seeing her there, had fallen in love with her. That was the way all the Aubignys fell in love, as if struck by a pistol shot. The wonder was that he had not loved her before; for he had known her since his father brought him home from Paris, a boy of eight, after his mother died there. The passion that awoke in him that day, when he saw her at the gate, swept along like an avalanche, or like a prairie fire, or like anything that drives headlong over all obstacles.
paragraphs.ja: ある日、彼女が、十八年前にその陰で眠っていたあの石の門柱にもたれて立っていたとき、馬で通りかかったアルマン・オービニーがそこにいる彼女を見て恋に落ちたのも、不思議ではなかった。オービニー家の者はみな、そういうふうに恋に落ちるのだった。まるでピストルで撃たれたかのように。むしろ不思議なのは、彼がそれまで彼女を愛さなかったことである。というのも彼は、母親がパリで亡くなったあと、八歳の少年のときに父親に連れられてパリから帰って来て以来、ずっと彼女を知っていたのだから。門のところで彼女を見たその日、彼の中に目覚めた情熱は、雪崩のように、あるいは大草原の野火のように、あるいはどんな障害もものともせずにまっしぐらに突き進むあらゆるもののように、猛然と押し寄せた。

paragraphs.en: Monsieur Valmonde grew practical and wanted things well considered: that is, the girl's obscure origin. Armand looked into her eyes and did not care. He was reminded that she was nameless. What did it matter about a name when he could give her one of the oldest and proudest in Louisiana? He ordered the corbeille from Paris, and contained himself with what patience he could until it arrived; then they were married.
paragraphs.ja: ヴァルモンド氏は現実的になり、物事をよく考えてほしいと望んだ。つまり、娘の素性がわからないことを、である。アルマンは彼女の目をのぞき込み、そんなことは気にしなかった。彼女には家名がないのだと念を押されもした。ルイジアナで最も古く、最も誇り高い名の一つを彼女に与えてやれるというのに、名前のことなど何の問題になろうか。彼はパリに婚礼の贈り物一式（コルベイユ）を注文し、それが届くまでできるかぎりの辛抱をしてはやる気持ちを抑えた。そして二人は結婚した。

paragraphs.en: Madame Valmonde had not seen Desiree and the baby for four weeks. When she reached L'Abri she shuddered at the first sight of it, as she always did. It was a sad looking place, which for many years had not known the gentle presence of a mistress, old Monsieur Aubigny having married and buried his wife in France, and she having loved her own land too well ever to leave it. The roof came down steep and black like a cowl, reaching out beyond the wide galleries that encircled the yellow stuccoed house. Big, solemn oaks grew close to it, and their thick-leaved, far-reaching branches shadowed it like a pall. Young Aubigny's rule was a strict one, too, and under it his negroes had forgotten how to be gay, as they had been during the old master's easy-going and indulgent lifetime.
paragraphs.ja: ヴァルモンド夫人がデジレと赤ん坊に会うのは四週間ぶりだった。ラブリに着くと、いつもそうなるように、ひと目見たとたんに身震いした。そこは陰気な感じのする場所で、もう何年ものあいだ、女主人のやさしい存在を知らずにきた。先代のオービニー氏はフランスで妻をめとり、そこで妻を葬ったのであり、妻のほうは自分の国をあまりに愛していたので、一度もそこを離れようとしなかったのである。屋根は修道士の頭巾のように急な傾きで黒々と垂れ下がり、黄色い漆喰塗りの家をぐるりと囲む広いベランダの先まで張り出していた。大きくいかめしいオークの木々がすぐそばに生えていて、葉の生い茂った、遠くまで伸びる枝が、棺を覆う布のように家に影を落としていた。若いオービニーの支配もまた厳しいもので、そのもとで彼の黒人たちは陽気にふるまうことを忘れてしまっていた。先代の主人が存命で、のんきで甘かったころには、陽気だったのだが。

paragraphs.en: The young mother was recovering slowly, and lay full length, in her soft white muslins and laces, upon a couch. The baby was beside her, upon her arm, where he had fallen asleep, at her breast. The yellow nurse woman sat beside a window fanning herself.

But I know it isn't true. I know he says that to please me. And mamma," she added, drawing Madame Valmonde's head down to her, and speaking in a whisper, "he hasn't punished one of them—not one of them—since baby is born. Even Negrillon, who pretended to have burnt his leg that he might rest from work—he only laughed, and said Negrillon was a great scamp. Oh, mamma, I'm so happy; it frightens me."

paragraphs.en: What Desiree said was true. Marriage, and later the birth of his son had softened Armand Aubigny's imperious and exacting nature greatly. This was what made the gentle Desiree so happy, for she loved him desperately. When he frowned she trembled, but loved him. When he smiled, she asked no greater blessing of God. But Armand's dark, handsome face had not often been disfigured by frowns since the day he fell in love with her.

paragraphs.en: When the baby was about three months old, Desiree awoke one day to the conviction that there was something in the air menacing her peace. It was at first too subtle to grasp. It had only been a disquieting suggestion; an air of mystery among the blacks; unexpected visits from far-off neighbors who could hardly account for their coming. Then a strange, an awful change in her husband's manner, which she dared not ask him to explain. When he spoke to her, it was with averted eyes, from which the old love-light seemed to have gone out. He absented himself from home; and when there, avoided her presence and that of her child, without excuse. And the very spirit of Satan seemed suddenly to take hold of him in his dealings with the slaves. Desiree was miserable enough to die.
paragraphs.ja: 赤ん坊が生後三か月ほどになったころ、デジレはある日目を覚ますと、自分の平穏を脅かす何かが漂っていると確信した。それは初めのうち、つかみどころがないほどかすかなものだった。それまではただ、不安をかきたてる気配にすぎなかった。黒人たちのあいだに漂う謎めいた雰囲気。遠くの隣人たちの思いがけない訪問――しかも彼らは、なぜ来たのかをろくに説明できないのだった。それから、夫の態度に起こった奇妙な、恐ろしい変化。それがどういうことなのか、彼女は夫に尋ねる勇気がなかった。彼が彼女に話しかけるときは目をそらしていて、その目からは、かつての愛の光が消えてしまったように見えた。彼は家を空けるようになり、家にいるときは、言い訳ひとつせずに彼女と子どもを避けた。そして、奴隷たちを扱うときには、まさに悪魔そのものが突然彼にとりついたかのようだった。デジレは死んでしまいたいほどみじめだった。

paragraphs.en: She sat in her room, one hot afternoon, in her peignoir, listlessly drawing through her fingers the strands of her long, silky brown hair that hung about her shoulders. The baby, half naked, lay asleep upon her own great mahogany bed, that was like a sumptuous throne, with its satin-lined half-canopy. One of La Blanche's little quadroon boys—half naked too—stood fanning the child slowly with a fan of peacock feathers. Desiree's eyes had been fixed absently and sadly upon the baby, while she was striving to penetrate the threatening mist that she felt closing about her. She looked from her child to the boy who stood beside him, and back again; over and over. "Ah!" It was a cry that she could not help; which she was not conscious of having uttered. The blood turned like ice in her veins, and a clammy moisture gathered upon her face.
paragraphs.ja: ある暑い午後、彼女は化粧着姿で自分の部屋に座り、肩のあたりに垂れた長く絹のような茶色の髪の房を、ものうげに指のあいだにすべらせていた。赤ん坊は半裸で、彼女自身の大きなマホガニーのベッドの上で眠っていた。繻子の裏地を張った半天蓋のついたそのベッドは、豪華な玉座のようだった。ラ・ブランシュの小さなクアドルーンの男の子の一人が――これも半裸で――そばに立ち、クジャクの羽の扇でゆっくりと赤ん坊をあおいでいた。デジレの目は、ぼんやりと悲しげに赤ん坊に注がれていた。そのあいだ彼女は、自分のまわりに迫ってくるように感じられる不気味な霧の向こうを見通そうと、懸命になっていた。彼女はわが子から、そのそばに立っている少年へと目を移し、またわが子へと戻した。何度も、何度も。「ああ！」それは思わずもれた叫びだった。自分では声を上げたことにも気づいていなかった。血管の中の血が氷のように冷たくなり、顔にじっとりと冷たい汗がにじんだ。
